records.title: OIF #CAP Innovation: training and EUR 10,000 seed prizes for young francophone entrepreneurs (2nd call closed 10 May 2026)
records.organization: Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), Unité jeunesse et société civile
records.overview: Yearly call of the OIF for young people aged 18 to 34 from its member, associate and observer states who carry an innovative entrepreneurial project (education and skills, ecological transition, cultural and creative industries, social engagement). In the 2nd edition 100 laureates followed a structured support path in September 2026, 20 projects received a year of enhanced support and 8 grand laureates a EUR 10,000 seed prize each. The 2nd call closed on 10 May 2026; the pages read announce no 3rd call.
records.country: Online application (open to the OIF's member, associate and observer states)
records.program_dates: 2nd edition: call 21 April to 10 May 2026; support path in September 2026; jury 22 October 2026; 8 grand laureates announced 4 November 2026; one year of support for the 20 selected projects. Training format (online or in person) not stated on the pages read.
records.deadline_text: No call open on 21 November 2026. 2nd call, OIF news page: 'La date limite pour l'envoi des candidatures est fixée au 10 mai 2026'; the OIF call platform shows opening 21/04/2026 18:30 UTC, closing 10/05/2026 18:00 UTC and the status 'Clôturé'. 1st call: 'Vous avez jusqu'au 21 mai 2025 pour déposer votre candidature'.
records.expected_next_cycle: No 3rd call is announced on the pages read (21 November 2026). The OIF ran a 1st call that closed on 21 May 2025 and a 2nd call from 21 April to 10 May 2026.
funding_details: OIF news page of 4 November 2026: each of the eight grand laureates 'recevra un prix d'amorçage de 10 000 euros' in addition to a year of tailored support including mentoring and networking; the prize goes to 8 projects only, not to every participant

The 100 laureates of the 2nd edition follow a structured support path with thematic training modules in September 2026; the 20 best projects get enhanced OIF support for a year (the pages do not say who pays for the training or whether it is free)
No application fee is mentioned on the pages read

records.stipend: None; EUR 10,000 seed prize for each of the 8 grand laureates only

records.title: AUF IFAV: Incubateur Francophone Africain Virtuel, online pre-incubator for students and young graduates (2026 call closed 11 October 2026)
records.overview: Online pre-incubation programme of the AUF for students and young graduates of francophone Africa who carry an innovative idea with a strong social or environmental impact: online training, personalised coaching and mentoring, practical workshops and peer exchange, from the ideation phase to a viable business model. The 2026 call ran from 25 September to 11 October 2026 and is closed. An IFAV call also ran in 2025 (closing 1 September 2025, per a secondary source).

records.title: ACEP Next Generation Resource Governance Leaders Program (policy-research internship in Ghana; 11th cohort closed 21 June 2026)
records.overview: Internship of the Africa Centre for Energy Policy for young Africans residing in Africa and aged up to 32. Interns write research reports and policy briefs on Africa's energy and extractive sectors, support stakeholder engagement, programme planning, monitoring and evaluation and proposal writing, and follow training in resource governance, leadership and career skills. ACEP provides a stipend, lunch, coaching and mentorship, and for international participants accommodation and a return ticket to Ghana. The 11th cohort call closed on 21 June 2026; no later call is shown on the ACEP pages read.

records.title: Orange Corners RDC: free 10-month support programme for young Congolese entrepreneurs in Kinshasa (call expected December to January)
records.organization: Orange Corners RDC (programme deployed by Ingenious City, Kinshasa)
records.overview: Ten-month support programme for project holders and start-up founders in the DRC, aged 18 to 35 and Congolese, with an innovative business idea, concept or MVP in six target sectors (food security, environment and climate change, water access, green energy, local processing of mineral resources, digitalisation). It offers training, coaching and mentoring every two weeks, networking, free coworking space and help to find funding, at no participation fee; in-person in Kinshasa and online for the rest of the DRC. The organiser's page says applications open between December and January each year and the programme starts in mid-February.
records.program_dates: 10 months, starting mid-February (organiser's yearly rule). In-person in Kinshasa; online for entrepreneurs living elsewhere in the DRC.
records.deadline_text: No call announced on 21 November 2026. Organiser's yearly rule: 'Les applications au programme sont ouvertes entre décembre et janvier chaque année.' The page's APPLY NOW button points to a 2026 short link; the 8th cohort's call was announced on 12 February 2026 (ACP news agency), without a stated deadline.
records.expected_next_cycle: Organiser states a yearly window of December to January with a start in mid-February; no 2027 call is announced on the pages read (21 November 2026). The 8th cohort's call was announced on 12 February 2026, later than the stated window.
funding_details: Official page FAQ: 'Il n'y a pas de coûts ou de frais de participation au programme' (no participation costs or fees)
Free access to the coworking space during the support period; practical training, workshops, coaching and mentoring every two weeks, networking
'En tant que programme, Orange Corners ne finance pas directement': the programme does not give cash grants; it connects entrepreneurs to public and private funders

records.title: Echoing Green Fellowship: stipend of USD 100,000 over 18 months for early-stage social entrepreneurs (start with the free Talent Platform, first window closes 31 March 2027)
records.overview: Full-time Fellowship for social entrepreneurs at the start of their journey, with seed funding described as a stipend of USD 100,000 over 18 months (recoverable grants for for-profit organisations), leadership development, expert support and virtual and in-person convenings, in a community of more than 1,000 social innovators. Becoming a Fellow now starts with joining the free Talent Platform: a short profile with three essay questions, one founder per organisation. Only members are invited to apply when the Fellowship application opens (selection dates to be announced in early 2027). The first review window closes on 31 March 2027, with later windows tentatively in July and October 2027. The founder must have started the work ('not unstarted work') but need not be incorporated; the organiser welcomes any nationality and sets no educational requirement.
